comment: Rows of fixtures/cases.json on which the core (aprv.wasm) and the 0.7 Java implementation answer differently, as DECISIONS.md R20 records them. A row is {class, group}: class is what tools/differential/compare.mjs finds (reason, payload, verdict), group names the R20 row that explains it (groups below). A row that compare.mjs reports stale answers alike again; remove it here.

groups.signer-certificate-refusal-stage: The SignerInfo's own certificate is one a strict X.509 reader refuses (version 11, an extension twice, a corrupt extension). The core reads it as the signer's defect (INVALID_CERTIFICATE); Java refuses every undecodable embedded certificate as a defect of the envelope (MALFORMED). The case allows both.
groups.tolerant-envelope-decoding: A genuinely signed envelope that is not valid DER elsewhere (the certificates field twice, an extensions field twice). OpenSSL decodes the whole ContentInfo (and each x5c certificate) with its templates and refuses; BouncyCastle reads only what it needs and verifies. The case allows both; the core fails closed. Malformed signed or unsigned attributes in one SignerInfo beside one that verifies left this group on 2026-10-06, when Java began reading every SignerInfo's attributes before trying any (Q65), and returned on 2026-10-12, when that pre-read was dropped (owner, Q107): BouncyCastle reads attributes only while verifying, so the broken SignerInfo is INVALID_SIGNATURE and the genuine one decides, while OpenSSL refuses a SignedData whose SignerInfo does not parse. The cases allow both.
groups.certificate-signature-in-chunks: An embedded certificate's outer signature BIT STRING, outside the signed TBS, in two chunks whose second has no initial octet of its own. OpenSSL joins the chunks' contents and verifies the same signature; BouncyCastle reads it as X.690 8.6.4 does, as a BIT STRING claiming 150 unused bits, and answers MALFORMED. The case allows both; the chain is judged either way.
groups.ber-forms-apple-never-emits: A BER form Apple's DER receipts never take: a string re-chunked into seven constructed levels, in the eContent, the Xcode wrap, an attribute value, or one SEQUENCE deep in a fourth field or an unsigned attribute value; a constructed UTCTime; a value whose length takes five octets. OpenSSL joins at most six chunk levels (ASN1_MAX_STRING_NEST), joins a constructed string of any type and reads the long length. BouncyCastle joins OCTET STRING chunks at any depth within its own nesting bound, builds no constructed UTCTime and reads the long length. The cases allow both, and the five-octet case pins only the raw octets both read; the signature and the chain are judged either way (R20, 2026-09-30, by the rule OD-17 applied to the two-chunk signature).
groups.nesting-between-33-and-bouncycastle: ASN.1 nested 33 deep, past the core's depth bound of 32 and within BouncyCastle's (org.bouncycastle.asn1.max_cons_depth, 64 by default): in the signed content, in an unsigned attribute value, the digestAlgorithms parameters, a crls entry or an embedded certificate's parameters, with SEQUENCEs or [0] context tags. The core refuses (UNREADABLE_PAYLOAD for the content, MALFORMED for the envelope); Java's only nesting bound is BouncyCastle's, so it verifies. Apple's receipts nest 9 deep. The cases allow both (R20, 2026-10-01).
groups.json-bounds-java-only: JSON a bounded reader refuses and serde_json reads: a JWS header member name of 50,001 characters, a header integer of 1,001 digits. The core reads each document into a map of raw member values, so a value nobody reads is skipped with no length bound, and the genuinely signed input verifies. Java reads under Jackson's default constraints (names 50,000, numbers 1,000) and refuses (MALFORMED). Apple's headers carry no such member. The cases allow both (R20 and R40, 2026-10-01). The three inputs nested 65 deep left this group on 2026-10-05, when Java dropped BoundedJson's depth of 64 for Jackson's 1,000 and both read them.
groups.negative-year-rendering: A receipt date of year 0000 renders its _pst time in the year -1: java.time prints -0001, jiff prints -001. The instant and every other field agree; no Apple receipt carries such a date (R20, 2026-10-07).
groups.dates-beyond-jiffs-calendar: A receipt date whose offset moves the instant past 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z or before 0000-01-01T00:00:00Z. Java reads it (a long holds the instant; owner, 2026-10-12); jiff's calendar ends at 9999, so the core keeps the attribute raw. Only informational dates are read after trust; a creation date like it moves the chain instant to where no certificate is valid on both sides (R20, 2026-10-12).
groups.self-issued-ca-without-key-identifiers: A receipt whose signer sits seven certificates below a pinned root, the last CA self-issued (its issuer's name, a fresh key), no certificate carrying key identifiers, every link signed under the root and valid at the instant. BouncyCastle 1.86's builder returns the path and Java verifies (owner, 2026-10-12, Q120 a). Without key identifiers OpenSSL's issuer lookup cannot tell the self-issued CA from its same-named issuer, takes the first and never backtracks, so the signer's signature fails under the wrong key; offered the self-issued CA first, OpenSSL reads it as self-signed and ends the path short of the root. The core answers UNTRUSTED_CHAIN whatever the length (measured 2026-10-12). The case allows both; Apple's certificates carry key identifiers (R20, 2026-10-12).
groups.path-length-java-builder-bound: A receipt whose signer sits eight certificates below a pinned root, every CA with its own name and key, every link signed under the root and valid at the instant. Neither implementation bounds the length of its own (owner, 2026-10-12, Q120 a and Q126 b). The core's path is bounded only by the ten-certificate cap, within OpenSSL's default depth of 100, and it verifies; BouncyCastle 1.86's builder, under the JDK's default maxPathLength of 5, returns no path of eight, and Java answers UNTRUSTED_CHAIN. The case allows both; Apple signs no receipt this deep (R20, 2026-10-12).
groups.committed-module-predates-the-core-chang: Rows the committed aprv.wasm (the last release's core) still answers differently from Java while the core on main no longer does. The differential runs the committed module, so these rows stay until the release tooling refreshes the pins (AGENTS.md); then compare.mjs reports them stale and they are removed. receipt/accept-a-path-of-seven: the committed core still bounds the walk at six (removed on 2026-10-12, Q126 b) and answers UNTRUSTED_CHAIN; Java and the core on main verify.
